references.text: The immediate context for Jesus' answer: the question of whether it was lawful to pay taxes to the emperor ([ref:Luk 20:22|Luke 20:22]).
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus gives the same answer: "Give therefore to the emperor what belongs to the emperor, and to God what belongs to God" ([ref:Matt 22:21|Matthew 22:21]).
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus answers with the same words about giving to the emperor what belongs to the emperor and to God what belongs to God ([ref:Mark 12:17|Mark 12:17]).

Paul urges believers to give everyone what they owe: taxes to those who collect taxes, tolls to those who collect tolls, respect and honor to those due it – in line with Jesus' principle of giving the emperor what belongs to the emperor ([ref:Rom 13:7|Romans 13:7]).

Paul teaches that everyone must submit to governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God. This expands on the principle Jesus formulated regarding the relationship between civic duty and worship ([ref:Rom 13:1-2|Romans 13:1-2]).
Peter urges Christians to submit to every human institution for the Lord's sake, whether it be the emperor or other authorities, while living as servants of God ([ref:1 Pet 2:13-17|1 Peter 2:13-17]).

The great commandment to love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength – the foundation for "give to God what belongs to God", meaning that the whole person belongs to God ([ref:5 Mos 6:5|Deuteronomy 6:5]).

God says about Cyrus: "I have anointed him ... for the sake of my servant Jacob." God uses earthly rulers in His plan, showing that political power and God's sovereignty are not opposed to each other ([ref:Jes 45:1|Isaiah 45:1]).

Human beings are created in God's image. Just as a coin bears the emperor's image and therefore belongs to the emperor, humans bear God's image and therefore belong to God – the basis for giving to God what belongs to God ([ref:1 Mos 1:27|Genesis 1:27]).

"The king's heart is like streams of water in the Lord's hand; He directs it wherever He wills." All earthly power is subject to God's sovereignty, which supports Jesus' teaching on the relationship between civic duty and obedience to God ([ref:Ordsp 21:1|Proverbs 21:1]).
